attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No theorem converts an arbitrary small circuit for the parity of SAT labels on generated queries into a constructively label-free low-support incidence sketch with subthreshold residual cost.
steps: Write H_N as the F_2 inner product of the generated incidence vector a_N(x) with the SAT label vector y_N.
Assume a subthreshold circuit D_N of size N^{1+epsilon-delta} computes H_N and try to use its gate transcript as T_N with P_N equal to the final gate.
This immediately violates label-freeness: D_N may encode information about y_N or about the carrier truth table, even if it never explicitly queries SAT.
Try expanding D_N as an algebraic normal form over seed bits or incidence coordinates; the support can blow up to 2^{S} and gives no N^{1+epsilon} threshold preservation.
Try quotienting incidences by syntactic SAT-preserving symmetries; this gives useful upper-bound falsifiers but not an extraction from arbitrary circuits.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The target-preserving bridge is valid and the sketch upper bound is a real falsifier, but proving absence of label-free sketches is weaker than proving C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} unless the nonrelativizing extraction theorem is supplied.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Constructive Label-Free Sketch Gate for XOR Magnification

assumptions: G_N outputs m_N=N^q formulas of length L_N=(log N)^d and has circuit size N^{rho+o(1)} including addressing overhead.
The incidence vector a_N(x) records generated formulas modulo two in the finite generated universe U_N, and y_N is the SAT truth vector on U_N.
T_N:{0,1}^N -> F_2^{r_N} has total circuit cost S_T and is constructively label-free.
P_N(T_N(x)) agrees with H_N(x) except on at most E_N seeds, and exceptional seeds may be patched by equality gates of cost O(E_N N).
definitions: source object: H_N:{0,1}^N -> {0,1} is the XOR of m_N=N^q generated SAT instances F_{N,j}(x) of length L_N=(log N)^d; the source model is nonuniform Boolean circuits SIZE and the weak lower bound is C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon}.
target object: Boolean SAT on formulas of length n; the target consequence is SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for every constant c, hence NP not subset P/poly by standard nonuniform completeness.

controlled interface: a generator G_N of size N^{rho+o(1)} produces the m_N query formulas, and target SAT circuits are substituted only at these generated query sites with every N^q, N^rho, and L_N^c cost charged.

target-preserving condition: d>1 and max{rho,q}<1+epsilon; every transcript used as a source falsifier is constructively label-free, excluding SAT truth labels, a circuit for H_N, or output-dependent advice.

constructively label-free transcript: T_N is produced by a fixed syntactic compiler from N, G_N, and named quotient/incidence maps; its description is not chosen using the SAT truth vector y_N or the truth table of H_N.

sparse quotient-polynomial sketch: P_N over F_2 has support A_N in its algebraic normal form and is evaluated on r_N transcript bits; coefficients may be nonuniform advice depending on real SAT labels, making the upper-bound falsifier stronger.

equations.label: xor-incidence-form
equations.valid_when: Valid when G_N outputs m_N length-L_N formulas and a_N records their mod-two incidences in the generated universe.

equations.label: label-free-sketch-upper-bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when T_N is constructively label-free, P_N has A_N monomials, and equality gates patch exactly E_N exceptional seeds.

equations.label: target-substitution-upper-bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after the generator has size N^{rho+o(1)} and every generated query has polylogarithmic length L_N.

equations.label: magnification-threshold
equations.valid_when: Requires the lower bound to hold infinitely often against nonuniform circuits and fixed q,rho below the threshold.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a constructively label-free T_N and sparse P_N with S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}; that is a valid falsifier of the proposed source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma preserves the route-level target bridge and formalizes a concrete falsifier class for the XOR carrier source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the polylog-query XOR-SAT carrier, constructively label-free sparse quotient-polynomial sketches are valid upper-bound falsifiers, while the target bridge remains max{rho,q}<1+epsilon. If such a sketch has S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}, then the claimed source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} is false. If the source lower bound is proved directly for infinitely many N under the same parameters, then SAT is not in P/poly.

assumptions: The transcript class contains all one-output circuits up to the tested size bound.
The sketch audit measures only existence of T_N and P_N, not how T_N was obtained from the generator.
definitions: unrestricted transcript: any nonuniform circuit family of the allowed size may be used as T_N, without a uniform syntactic compiler or label-free restriction.
output-dependent leakage: the description of T_N may depend on SAT labels, the carrier truth table, or a small circuit for H_N.
collapse certificate: T_N(x)=H_N(x), r_N=1, and P_N(z)=z.

equations.label: trivial-transcript
equations.valid_when: Valid when the transcript definition allows output-dependent nonuniform advice or arbitrary carrier circuits.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the proposed transcript class admits T_N=H_N, the route has a leakage falsifier and must be rejected.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This quarantines unrestricted sparse-sketch lower bounds as non-contribution-making for the source problem.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Unrestricted nonuniform transcript classes collapse the sparse-sketch audit. If the transcript may be chosen with output-dependent advice or may contain an arbitrary small circuit for H_N, then T_N=H_N and P(z)=z form a one-bit sketch, so sketch hardness is merely the original general-circuit lower bound in disguise.

assumptions: There is a circuit D_N of size at most N^{1+epsilon-delta} computing H_N.
The extraction is required to output T_N from the generator and syntactic SAT structure, not from D_N as label-dependent advice.
The parameters satisfy max{rho,q}<1+epsilon and d>1 so the target bridge itself is not the bottleneck.
definitions: extraction theorem: a real-SAT-specific transformation from an arbitrary small circuit computing H_N into a low-cost constructively label-free sketch.
nonrelativizing requirement: the transformation must use structure of Boolean satisfiability, not merely oracle access to the SAT label vector.
residual charge: exceptions and non-sketchable behavior must be bounded by E_N N below the N^{1+epsilon} threshold.

equations.label: needed-extraction-template
equations.latex: C(H_N)\le N^{1+\epsilon-\delta}\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists(T_N,P_N,E_N):\ S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N\le N^{1+\epsilon-o(1)}.
equations.valid_when: Would be valid only after proving a real-SAT nonrelativizing extraction from arbitrary circuits to label-free incidence transcripts.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Construct an oracle or advice-leakage model where H_N has small circuits but no uniform label-free incidence sketch below threshold.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This names the remaining proof obligation separating sketch falsifier search from an actual source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A lower bound against constructively label-free sketches is not yet a lower bound for C(H_N). Promotion needs a nonrelativizing extraction theorem: every subthreshold circuit for H_N must yield a subthreshold constructively label-free incidence transcript plus a sparse polynomial and patchable residual.

control_decision.pivot_test: If no enforceable label-free transcript class yields new falsifiers beyond known incidence symmetries, pivot from sketch audits to direct lower bounds for H_N or to a different carrier.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after proving either C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} directly for an explicit XOR carrier or the extraction theorem from arbitrary small H_N circuits to subthreshold constructively label-free sketches.
control_decision.reason: The branch made route-level progress by naming the exact leakage gate and preserving the quantitative target bridge, while avoiding any claim that P != NP follows.

dependency_updates.description: The XOR carrier still magnifies an i.o. N^{1+epsilon} lower bound to SAT notin P/poly when d>1 and max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
Transcript classes must be generated by a syntactic compiler independent of SAT labels and H_N; semantic nonuniform independence is not enough.
Allowing output-dependent or SAT-label-dependent advice in T_N admits the one-bit T_N=H_N collapse.
To turn sketch lower bounds into source lower bounds, prove a nonrelativizing extraction from arbitrary small H_N circuits to constructively label-free incidence sketches.
Any T_N,P_N,E_N with S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N below threshold remains a concrete falsifier for the proposed source lower bound.

falsifiers: Output-dependent transcript leakage: T_N=H_N makes sparse-sketch hardness vacuous.
SAT-label advice in the transcript compiler below the tested threshold invalidates label-freeness.
Constructively label-free T_N with S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} is a direct source lower-bound falsifier.
Symmetry-pair cancellation after SAT-preserving quotienting can make a high-entropy XOR carrier constant or sparse.
Threshold collapse occurs if max{rho,q}>=1+epsilon, since SAT substitution no longer contradicts the source lower bound.
Lookup collapse reappears for d<=1 when the generated truth-table cost can fall below the claimed source threshold.
A relativizing extraction attempt is blocked if small H_N circuits use oracle/advice correlations not recoverable from incidence structure.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For alpha near 1+epsilon, any subthreshold circuit for H_N can be placed into the transcript advice, recreating the T=H_N collapse. With alpha=0 or polylog-uniform advice, sketches become genuine upper-bound falsifiers, but extraction from arbitrary H_N circuits becomes the missing nonrelativizing step.
held_fixed_controls: The SAT substitution bridge is held fixed with d=2 and max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
The source lower-bound target remains C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} against general nonuniform circuits.
P_N coefficients may hardwire SAT labels after the label-free transcript is fixed.
Equality patching costs E_N N gates and must stay below threshold.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route now hinges on whether label-free is a mathematically enforceable interface or just a verbal ban on T=H_N. A concrete leakage experiment tests the exact threshold at which the sketch audit collapses into the original circuit lower bound.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: High-q XOR-SAT carrier with L_N=(log N)^2, q in ((1+epsilon)/2,1+epsilon), rho<1+epsilon, and H_N(x)=xor_j SAT(F_{N,j}(x)); transcripts are generated by a compiler that may receive b_N bits of auxiliary advice.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: An advice-accounted label-free sketch lemma plus a formal compiler-independence condition; promotion further needs a real-SAT extraction theorem mapping every small H_N circuit to a low-advice incidence transcript without threshold loss.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: Advice leakage exponent alpha where b_N=N^alpha bits may be used by the transcript compiler.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 60 separates two notions previously conflated. Sparse quotient-polynomial sketches are valid upper-bound falsifiers only when the transcript is constructively label-free; otherwise T_N=H_N collapses the audit. The target bridge max{rho,q}<1+epsilon survives, but sketch-hardness is not a source lower bound without a nonrelativizing extraction theorem or a direct C(H_N) lower bound.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Define the first concrete compiler class T^{inc-lin}: T_N(x)=B_N a_N(x) for explicit SAT-preserving quotient matrices B_N of row sparsity polylog N, then compute the minimum S_T+A_N r_N for representing H_N by sparse P_N in the high-q, d=2 regime.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Missing target-preserving compiler from polynomial-time or size-m^k SAT deciders to branching programs of size at most 2^{O(m)} or poly(m); such a compiler would be a major P-to-L/poly compression and is not supplied by the route.
steps: Let f_m=SAT_m and suppose a source theorem proves BP(f_m)>L(m).
To refute SIZE(m^k), contraposition must certify that every size-m^k circuit for f_m yields a branching program of size below L(m).
The known circuit-to-BP conversion gives only BP(f_m)<=2^{O(m^k)}poly(m).
Therefore the source lower bound would need L(m)>2^{O(m^k)} for the transfer to be valid.
But every total m-bit function satisfies BP(f_m)<=2^{m+1}-1, so the needed threshold is impossible for k>1.
The derivation can validly separate SAT from L/poly if L(m) is superpolynomial, but that is not a P != NP consequence.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This certifies failure of one BP-mediated route only. It does not prove SAT in P or SAT outside P, and it does not rule out lower-bound methods that avoid BP as the carrier.

assumptions: BP is unrestricted, deterministic, nonuniform, and queries ordinary input bits.
Circuits are fan-in two Boolean circuits of size s=m^k unless stated otherwise.
The transfer uses only the known configuration evaluation of a time-bounded machine or circuit.
No unproved compression from P computations to polynomial-size branching programs is assumed.
definitions: source object: BP(f_m), the minimum size of an unrestricted deterministic branching program computing the total m-bit slice f_m=SAT_m or a padded SAT slice.
target object: DTIME(m^k) or nonuniform SIZE(m^k) lower bounds for SAT_m; polynomial-size BP lower bounds by themselves target L/poly-like models.
controlled interface: compile a T-time machine or size-s Boolean circuit for f_m into a branching program, then compare the resulting BP upper bound with the claimed source lower bound.
target-preserving condition: the compiler bound B_T(m) or B_s(m) must be asymptotically below the proved BP lower bound on the same input length and padding slice, with no advice or promise leakage.

equations.label: decision_tree_ceiling
equations.valid_when: Valid when BP is unrestricted and the function is total on all m-bit inputs, so the full decision tree may be used.

equations.label: time_to_bp
equations.valid_when: Valid for a fixed multitape Turing-machine model whose configurations use O(T(m)) work bits and halt within T(m) steps.

equations.label: circuit_to_bp
equations.valid_when: Applies after a size-s circuit is evaluated by a deterministic configuration process with O(s) stored gate values and hardwired circuit description.

equations.label: pnp_threshold_collapse
equations.valid_when: Requires the target transfer to use the known exponential circuit-to-BP compiler and compares it with the universal m-bit decision-tree ceiling.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proposed BP route fails if its only transfer from P or SIZE(m^k) to BP uses a 2^{O(m^k)} bound while the source measure is capped by 2^m.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-failure bridge: the measure is valid for BP or L/poly targets, but not for P != NP transfer through this interface.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Unrestricted deterministic branching-program lower bounds for SAT_m cannot transfer to P or SIZE(m^k) through the standard configuration/circuit simulation: for every k>1 the required BP lower bound exceeds the universal decision-tree ceiling.

assumptions: The machine halts within T(m) steps and uses S(m) work space.
Input-head location and finite control are included in the configuration count.
Advice, if present, is fixed for length m and hardwired into the BP family.
definitions: source object: BP(f_m) for a total Boolean slice f_m on m bits.
target object: deterministic time T(m), space S(m) machines, and their nonuniform L/poly analogues.
controlled interface: represent machine configurations as BP nodes and input-dependent transitions as BP edges.
target-preserving condition: the lower bound must exceed the configuration count on the same length m, including advice and padding parameters.

equations.label: space_time_to_bp
equations.valid_when: Valid when the deterministic computation has an explicit time bound T and every reachable configuration uses at most S work bits.

equations.label: logspace_poly_bp
equations.valid_when: Applies to logspace polynomial-time machines after advice and transition tables are fixed for each input length.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the target algorithm may use polynomial workspace, the BP upper bound becomes exponential in m^k and the transfer is invalid for P.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repair lemma: promotes BP lower bounds only for classes with certified small configuration graphs.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Branching-program lower bounds do transfer to small-space targets: if BP(f_m) exceeds the configuration bound of a T-time S-space computation, then f_m is not in that time-space class; this is a valid route for L/poly-style separations, not P-vs-NP.

assumptions: Branching program encodings choose a queried variable and two outgoing arcs per node.
Truth-table length is N=2^m.
Constructivity is measured in time polynomial in N.
definitions: source object: property P_s={truth tables f in {0,1}^{2^m}: BP(f)>s}.
target object: BP-size-s families or L/poly-like classes, not unrestricted SIZE(m^k).
controlled interface: count all size-s branching programs and enumerate them against the N-bit truth table.
target-preserving condition: usefulness must be against a class whose members all have BP size at most s.

equations.label: bp_count
equations.valid_when: Valid when each BP node is encoded by one input variable index and two successor pointers among O(s) nodes.

equations.label: largeness
equations.valid_when: Valid for uniformly random total m-bit Boolean functions after applying the union bound over encoded size-s branching programs.

equations.label: constructivity_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the algorithm enumerates all candidate BPs and evaluates each on the entire N-bit truth table.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Do not cite natural-proof escape as progress unless usefulness is against SIZE(m^k); high BP is not useful against general circuits at polynomial s.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit: near-linear BP lower-bound properties can naturalize for BP targets, but superlinear BP thresholds evade this enumeration audit without solving the P-transfer gap.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The high-BP property is large, but its simple enumeration constructivity is poly(N) only near the s log(sm)=O(m) threshold for N=2^m; hence natural-proof obstruction is scoped and the decisive P-transfer obstruction remains quantitative.

control_decision.pivot_test: If a future BP route cannot provide a subexponential P-to-BP compiler on the same padded length, pivot to restricted BP targets or quarantine it.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only when the target class C has an explicit bound BP(C_m)<=B_C(m) below the proposed lower bound, such as logspace, OBDD, read-k BP, or bounded-width BP.
control_decision.reason: The branch obtained a named source model, target model, compiler interface, and impossible threshold. BP lower bounds are promoted only where the target has certified small configuration graphs.

dependency_updates.description: Known time/circuit-to-BP compilers are exponential in time or circuit size, so P-vs-NP transfer demands BP lower bounds above the universal m-bit ceiling.
High-BP properties are large and poly(N)-constructive only when s log(sm)=O(m); for larger s, naturalness is not the decisive obstruction, but usefulness against full circuits still fails.
The route uses nonuniform truth-table lower bounds and gives no nonrelativizing mechanism; however the immediate obstruction is quantitative target collapse rather than an oracle contradiction.
No algebraic extension or low-degree oracle interface is used in this BP carrier, so algebrization is outside the present failure certificate.

falsifiers: Full decision tree falsifier: every total m-bit function has BP size below 2^{m+1}, so no unrestricted BP lower bound can exceed the 2^{Omega(m^k)} threshold needed for k>1 through the standard compiler.
Target falsifier: a polynomial BP lower bound for SAT is valid against L/poly-like models but says nothing about polynomial-time algorithms with polynomial workspace.
Padding falsifier: PadSAT_{ell,beta}(x,z)=SAT_ell(x) preserves NP-hardness under padding while its BP ceiling follows the ell-bit core, eroding any padding-insensitive BP transfer.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: BP(PadSAT_{ell,beta})<=2^{ell+1}+O(m)=2^{m^{1/beta}+O(log m)}, while the known SIZE(m^k)-to-BP transfer would require a lower bound above 2^{Omega(m^k)}. Increasing beta widens the gap and exposes non-target-preservation.
held_fixed_controls: Source measure is unrestricted deterministic BP size on the total m-bit truth table.
Target class is SIZE(m^k) or DTIME(m^k) for a fixed k>1.
The reduction preserves SAT hardness syntactically and introduces no promise on padding bits.
The only allowed transfer is a named BP compiler with explicit size bound and no hidden advice leakage.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: Unrestricted BP size has a universal 2^m ceiling, while the P/SIZE transfer through configurations asks for a 2^{m^k} lower bound. A concrete padded slice tests whether the route preserves the target parameter or merely proves a small-space separation.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: PadSAT_{ell,beta}(x,z)=SAT_ell(x) on m=ell^beta input bits, with z ignored and the standard reduction x -> (x,0^{m-ell}).
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A theorem showing that every SIZE(m^k) or DTIME(m^k) decider for the padded slice induces a BP of size below the proved lower bound, preferably poly(m) or 2^{o(m)}. Without this, the experiment is only a valid falsifier for the BP route.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 60 isolates unrestricted BP size as a valid carrier for small-space or L/poly lower bounds but not for P != NP. The bridge to P/SIZE requires an exponential-in-m^k BP lower bound, while every m-bit function has BP size O(2^m). This is a quantitative threshold-collapse falsifier, not evidence about the main conjecture.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit read-k and bounded-width branching programs: compute the exact B_C(m,k,w) compiler thresholds for NC1, logspace, and AC0 targets, and reject any unrestricted P claim without such a certificate.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No construction is known for the required generated anti-ball source: it must give a sparse, advice-free, non-natural proof that some generated row is far from every unrestricted circuit of size 2^{theta m}.
steps: Let U_m be the E-canonical list of distinct generated rows with |U_m|=M_m<=2^{D m+o(m)}.
Define L on padded length n_m by parsing an input as a rank r, an address x in {0,1}^m, and padding, and outputting the generated row bit T_{m,r}(x).
Because unranking and row/proof generation take 2^{O(m)} time and n_m=Theta(m), L is in E; long but constant-exponential generated proofs only change the hidden E time constant.
Assume a circuit family for L of size 2^{delta n_m}. Fix the rank bits to a hard row r* certified by the source theorem. The restricted circuit computes T_{m,r*} with size 2^{delta n_m}+poly(n_m).
If delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)), then for large m this size is below 2^{theta m}, contradicting the anti-ball MCSP soundness of T_{m,r*}.
If generation time is instead 2^{a(m)m} with a(m)->infinity, keeping L in E requires n_m=Omega(a(m)m), so the same inequality yields only delta=o(1).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The extraction theorem is conditional and valid only after the source theorem is supplied. The missing source theorem is essentially a global unrestricted circuit lower-bound certificate, so this is route-level progress rather than progress on P != NP itself.

assumptions: For each source length m in a kappa-dense sequence, there are at most M_m=2^{D m+o(m)} distinct generated rows after E-canonical quotienting.

There exists at least one row r* at length m with C(T_{m,r*})>2^{theta m}; easy contamination among other rows is allowed because multiplexing fixes the hard rank after a hypothetical circuit for L is given.
The generator is uniform and advice-free; any proof object is produced by the generator in constant-exponential time and is not an external witness to be searched for.
The target circuit model is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits; restricted lower bounds or uniform-only hardness do not certify MCSP no-side soundness.
definitions: source object: an E-uniform generated anti-ball MCSP carrier {T_{m,r}} with N=2^m truth-table length, distinct row entropy Dm+o(m), and at least one generated row having unrestricted circuit complexity greater than 2^{theta m}.
target object: a language L in E obtained by multiplexing row rank r and address x, with target lower bound against nonuniform SIZE(2^{delta n}) circuits on kappa-dense padded lengths.
controlled interface: rank-unranking multiplexing computes L(r,x,pad)=T_{m,r}(x), while proof streams witnessing anti-ball soundness are generated deterministically and never supplied as advice.

target-preserving condition: row generation and proof generation take 2^{O(m)} time, source lengths are kappa-dense, distinct images have entropy Dm+o(m), and anti-ball soundness is against unrestricted Boolean circuits.

equations.label: row-count
equations.valid_when: Valid when duplicates are removed by an E-canonical distinct-image unranking procedure.

equations.label: target-length
equations.valid_when: Valid when source length gaps are absorbed only by padding and rank bits.

equations.label: source-hardness
equations.valid_when: Valid when the anti-ball proof excludes every unrestricted circuit of that size.

equations.label: extracted-bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after fixing rank bits preserves circuit size up to polynomial overhead.

equations.label: generation-budget
equations.valid_when: Requires deterministic generated proof streams and no advice for proof locations.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma fails if locating or generating the proof requires 2^{omega(m)} time, if the hard row is supplied by nonuniform advice, or if anti-ball soundness is only for a restricted circuit class.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This sharpens the route by proving that constant-exponential generated proofs do not reduce the lower-bound exponent; only row entropy D and padding kappa are charged.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A low-distinct-image, E-uniform generated anti-ball MCSP carrier with constant-exponential proof generation yields the same E lower-bound exponent as the earlier multiplexing bridge: for every delta < theta/(kappa(1+D)), the induced language L in E has no circuits of size 2^{delta n} on the target padded lengths. This is valid route-level transfer only, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: The row computation of L invokes the generator or an equivalent deterministic locator.
No alternative E-uniform shortcut computes the row bits without producing the expensive stream.
The source MCSP threshold remains 2^{theta m} with theta constant.
definitions: source model: generated MCSP carrier with row/proof generation exponent a(m).
target model: E lower bound with constant exponent delta against unrestricted circuits.
interface: increase padding until the generator runs within 2^{O(n)} time.
target preservation: delta must remain a positive constant independent of m.

equations.label: forced-padding
equations.valid_when: Valid when the target language must compute generated rows inside E time.

equations.label: collapse
equations.valid_when: Applies when source hardness is measured at length m and padding absorbs generation overhead.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If an independent E-uniform bit algorithm exists, the overhead parameter must be redefined using that algorithm rather than the proof stream.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a quantitative falsifier for generated-proof proposals that hide nonuniform search in superconstant exponential generation time.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the generated proof or row locator needs time 2^{a(m)m} with a(m)->infinity, then either the constructed language is not in E under linear padding, or padding must grow with a(m), causing the extracted exponent to collapse to o(1).

assumptions: Constructivity is measured in polynomial time in N=2^m when the entire truth table is given.
Usefulness means every accepted truth table has circuit complexity greater than 2^{theta m}.
The obstruction is conditional on the usual existence of exponentially secure pseudorandom functions.
definitions: source model: projection of generated row/proof pairs onto m-input truth tables.
target model: MCSP no-side carrier useful against unrestricted circuits of size 2^{theta m}.
interface: decidability of the projected row property as a property of full truth tables.
target preservation: the projection must stay sparse or nonconstructive enough to avoid natural-proof largeness and constructivity together.

equations.label: large-projection
equations.valid_when: Valid when largeness is measured over all Boolean truth tables of length N.

equations.label: sparse-carrier-measure
equations.valid_when: Applies to low-D generated carriers after quotienting duplicate emitted rows.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the projection is dense, poly(N)-decidable, and useful, it is a natural-proofs falsifier for this route unless the PRF assumption or usefulness premise is explicitly abandoned.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This certifies which locator repairs are blocked by the natural-proofs barrier and which sparse repairs remain only outside the known barrier, not proved sound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A projection repair that makes the row set polynomial-time decidable, useful against 2^{theta m}-size circuits, and large at density at least 2^{-poly(m)} becomes a natural-property object under standard pseudorandom-function assumptions; sparse generated carriers with measure 2^{-N+o(N)} avoid this specific barrier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every plausible generated anti-ball proof either requires superconstant exponential location or becomes a dense poly(N)-decidable useful projection.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a concrete no-advice generator and nonblackbox soundness proof certify a low-D row family with theta>0 against unrestricted circuits.
control_decision.reason: The bridge is now quantitatively stable under long generated proofs, and the next bottleneck is a source theorem rather than another transfer restatement.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier must be a low-D generated anti-ball family with at least one unrestricted hard row; easy contamination is allowed only through multiplexing.
Constant-exponential proof generation is not charged in the lower-bound exponent; the valid transfer remains delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
E-uniformity permits 2^{O(m)} generated row/proof streams but rejects 2^{omega(m)} location unless extra padding is paid, causing threshold collapse.
Dense poly(N)-decidable useful projections are quarantined; sparse generated projections of measure 2^{-N+o(N)} remain outside this barrier but still need soundness.
Need a nonblackbox, no-advice certificate excluding every unrestricted circuit below 2^{theta m}; black-box challenge lists remain invalid.

falsifiers: falsifier: proof or row location is supplied by nonuniform advice rather than generated uniformly
falsifier: generated proof time is 2^{omega(m)} and padding makes the extracted exponent vanish
falsifier: the anti-ball proof excludes only formulas, AC0, or uniform algorithms instead of unrestricted circuits
falsifier: indexed random access to row bits has circuit size below 2^{theta m-o(m)}
falsifier: dense polynomial-time projection of accepted rows creates a useful natural property
falsifier: black-box query certification uses q=o(2^{theta m}/m) table probes and cannot bind all small circuits
falsifier: source soundness relies on lex-first search through all truth tables, which is not E-uniform at the target length

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For constant lambda, L remains in E and the bound delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) is unchanged; for lambda(m)->infinity, either L leaves E or padding forces delta to o(1).
held_fixed_controls: MCSP threshold theta is a positive constant against unrestricted nonuniform circuits.
Distinct-image entropy D and padding density kappa are fixed constants.
The generator is deterministic, uniform, and advice-free.
The row decoder has no subthreshold indexed random access shortcut.
Projection of accepted rows remains sparse and not a natural-size property.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Use now as a falsifier probe for generated anti-ball source proposals.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch has a valid conditional MCSP-to-E bridge; the live uncertainty is whether proof generation overhead secretly destroys E-uniformity or the lower-bound exponent.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: A canonical low-D generated anti-ball family U_m of m-input truth tables, where each row has a sequential proof stream certifying distance from all circuits of size 2^{theta m}; the induced language multiplexes rank and address and pads to length n_m.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal E-uniform bit-generation algorithm for the multiplexed language plus a nonblackbox anti-ball soundness proof for at least one generated row at each kappa-dense source length.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: proof-generation exponent lambda in t_G(m)=2^{lambda m+o(m)}, with lambda either constant or slowly growing.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 60 separates proof length from proof-generation exponent. Generated anti-ball proofs may be exponentially long without weakening the MCSP-to-E transfer, but only with a constant exponent and advice-free generation. Superconstant generation overhead is a valid quantitative falsifier because preserving E then collapses the extracted exponent to o(1). The remaining source obligation is a sparse generated non-natural anti-ball certificate against unrestricted circuits.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate a toy generated anti-ball proof with D=0 or D=o(1), compute its row-decoder access profile, and test whether its soundness argument is genuinely nonblackbox or secretly a subthreshold challenge-list verifier.
